title: Open Editor: the Style menu and three views

fields.title: One Style menu, three views
fields.subtitle: Every style with its shortcut · Formatted, Markdown, HTML

beats.say: Two additions to the chapter editor. One menu for every style, and three ways to see and edit the same chapter.
A chapter is open. Every style is in one menu, each with its keyboard shortcut.
Choose a text style and it gets a tick. The menu stays open for the next one.
beats.label: styles *combine*

beats.say: Escape goes back to the text, and what is typed has both.
Now the same chapter as Markdown. This is not a preview. It is the chapter, and it can be edited here.
beats.label: the same chapter, as _Markdown_

beats.say: Switch back, and it is a heading.
beats.label: typed in Markdown, shown *formatted*

beats.say: And as HTML. A script typed here is dropped, and nothing in the text is ever run.
beats.text: And as HTML. A script typed here is dropped, and nothing in the text is ever run.
beats.label: the same chapter, as _HTML_

fields.title: A chapter survives the trip
fields.body: Formatted  →  Markdown  →  Formatted  ·  Formatted  →  HTML  →  Formatted

beats.say: A test takes each example chapter through the Markdown view and the HTML view. It must come back exactly as it went in: text, styles, footnotes and images.

fields.title: What it costs
fields.subtitle: The author workspace is two and a half times the size

beats.say: The price is size. The author workspace now carries a code editor and a Markdown parser. The guide has the numbers.
